subject: NimbleCart: short-window overspill bridge & uplift clarification
messages:
From: Asha Raman <asha.raman@nimblecart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short-window uplift for Black Friday test — pricing & PO flow

Ben / Lauren,

Quick one from procurement — we have a planned 72-hour load test next month to simulate Black Friday checkout volumes. We expect the run to generate a short spike (roughly +1.8M tokens/day over baseline for 3 days).

We need two things:
- A clear pricing path for a short-term quota uplift (how you charge for the uplift window vs normal rate).
- Confirmation of how overrun true-ups are billed retroactively and whether there are any cap/soft-limits we can use to avoid surprise invoices.

Our finance lead prefers a simple PO flow (PO -> invoice net30) rather than committing to a multi-month seat. Can you provide a short proposal with: uplift rate, any minimum commit, available temporary discount, and PO instructions?

Also flag if we need any SLA exception for the launch traffic.

Thanks,
Asha Raman
Head of Platform Ops, NimbleCart
procurement@nimblecart.com

--
NimbleCart

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Asha Raman <asha.raman@nimblecart.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-window uplift for Black Friday test — pricing & PO flow

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic plan. Short answer up front: we can support a short-window uplift with two practical options depending on your preference for predictability vs minimal upfront commitment. Details below.

Option A — Ephemeral uplift (no commit):
- Temporary quota increase for the defined window (72 hours).
- Billing: pay-as-you-go at our overrun rate: $0.0095 / 1k tokens (reduced from list $0.0125 for ephemeral bridge).
- No minimums or PO constraints; invoice after the window (net30).
- Automatic cap option available (you can set a soft cap to stop excessive spend).

Option B — Short provisional commit (preferred for predictability):
- Provisional add-on: 3-day uplift converted to a prorated short-term commit.
- Billing: blended rate $0.0075 / 1k tokens for uplifted volume; any usage above provisional commit billed at standard overrun ($0.0125).
- Requires a one-time purchase order referencing DEAL-7842.

Discount & negotiation notes:
- For customers doing a one-off test we can apply a one-time 15% uplift discount on Option B if you provide a PO before Sep 28.
- We can also include a single-day complimentary headroom (up to 500k tokens) to help with warm-up traffic profiling.

SLA and exceptions:
- No SLA change required for 72-hour tests. If you expect sustained production traffic beyond the test window, we recommend a Dedicated commit and an SLA addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you want Option A we can enable immediately and send a short confirmation email (no PO).
2) If you prefer Option B, send PO -> we’ll return a credit note and proforma invoice and schedule uplift.

I attached a concise uplift quote (nimblecart-uplift-quote-7842.pdf) and the SLA exception template in case procurement needs to review language.

If helpful I can jump on a 15-min call to run the math against your exact token estimates.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0162

From: Asha Raman <asha.raman@nimblecart.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-window uplift for Black Friday test — pricing & PO flow

Ben — thanks, that is helpful. A few clarifying questions inline:

> Option A — Ephemeral uplift (no commit): billing at $0.0095 / 1k tokens

1) Is the ephemeral rate a promotional price or part of standard overrun tiers? Will it be honored if the window moves by a week?

> Option B — Short provisional commit: blended $0.0075 / 1k tokens (requires PO)

2) With Option B, can the provisional commit be applied only to the uplifted delta (the +1.8M/day) or does it need to be a full account-level uplift? We prefer delta-only if possible.
3) Can you confirm the billing metric used for the uplift (generated tokens vs input+output)? We measure cost by generated tokens in our stack.

PO questions:
- Our PO team needs creditor details and a remit address on the proforma. Please include the correct legal entity and address on your invoice.

We are leaning toward Option B (delta-only) if you can do the 15% one-time discount and confirm generated-token billing. If you can send a short proforma with those details we’ll route approval today.

Thanks,
Asha

--

Asha — looping in to confirm and close this out quickly.

Answers to your questions:
- Ephemeral rate status: the $0.0095 / 1k tokens is a standard short-window overrun concession we offer for ad-hoc bridges; we can hold that pricing for bookings confirmed within 14 days of the requested uplift window.
- Delta-only provisional commit: yes — Option B can be delta-scoped. We’ll apply the provisional commit to the uplift delta (+1.8M/day) rather than overriding your account baseline.
- Billing metric: we bill on total generated tokens. If NimbleCart measures only generated tokens on your end, that will align with our meter. We’ll include the exact meter IDs in the proforma so your accounting can reconcile.

We’ve prepared a short proforma (attached) with the 15% one-time discount and our Redwood legal entity + remit instructions. For speed, reference DEAL-7842 on the PO and we’ll provision uplift within 24 hours of PO receipt.

DocuSign flow: we don’t require a signature for this uplift; a PO referencing DEAL-7842 is sufficient. If you need an MSA amendment we can provide one.

I attached the proforma and SLA template for your procurement team: redwood-sla-exception-template.docx (contains remit address).

If you’re ready I can have the billing team create the invoice as soon as the PO is in — ETA for provisioning after PO = 24 hours.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
